scope: 21 substantive native PvP arenas, including multiplayer and transparent PvP; excludes synthetic Dummy and separate single-player/ladder workflows

image_audit.architecture_scope: Actual image platforms verified; this does not claim runtime parity or native testing on other host architectures

audit_method: Independent read-only inspection of actual trial result, verifier reward/verification, native metadata, archived round results, and arena-specific raw match outcomes. No containers or models launched.
audit_notes: Harbor verifier pass and healthy competitive execution are separate observations.
Count arenas once; rounds, matches, attempts, and fixed baseline bots are not independent benchmark tasks.
Earlier failed attempts remain in the audit; recovering an infrastructure failure does not erase it.
No claim of adversarial grading isolation or model capability follows from smoke evidence.

verified_arenas and healthy_competitive_execution_arenas mean at least one audited attempt; latest_attempt fields exclude running or failed newest attempts. Source hashes must match any claimed final revision.

Healthy competitive execution means completed valid games, not correct per-player native score attribution. Halite2 and Halite3 inherit a confirmed zero-based/one-based player indexing defect; see native-scoring-caveats.json.

With the observed two players this swaps wins and native winner attribution. Completed games and replay equality do not establish correct player attribution.

source_references.finding: Halite2Arena inherits HaliteArena scoring without an override
Halite3 delegates get_results to the same inherited implementation with its own log pattern

native_scoring_caveats.recommendation: Disclose the attribution defect with all reported native scores. Any corrected scorer is a separate explicitly versioned upstream-fix experiment and requires renewed parity, not an unrecorded adapter change.

limitations: Diagnostic smoke verifies infrastructure and native execution, not model quality or parity.
Verifier consistency checks do not authenticate results against malicious code in the shared native arena.
A verifier-passed all-invalid/no-output run is not healthy competitive arena coverage; original Halite3 attempt retained and excluded.
Per-attempt source hashes retain pre-fix failures and recovery evidence; equivalent final Git batching is covered by RobotRumble recovery and a real-Git regression.
Native source revisions are pinned; some base images/toolchains and randomness remain unpinned.
Transparent Bridge retains native stale root snapshots with updated files nested under workspace; it does not prove root paths refresh.
Healthy competitive execution means completed valid games, not correct native score attribution: Halite2/Halite3 preserve an upstream scorer bug in all six audited rounds.
